objective: Developing a requirements management plan: stakeholders, roles/responsibilities, and elicitation/analysis/approval methods
secondaryObjectives: Defining a requirements traceability strategy using traceability tools and techniques
Defining business metrics and acceptance criteria collaboratively with stakeholders

sources.cite: PMI, Professional in Business Analysis (PMI-PBA) exam: Needs Assessment 18%, Planning 22%, Analysis 35%, Traceability and Monitoring 15%, Evaluation 10%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through summarizing fetches of two study pages: examcert.app (2026-08-16), which says its weights 'come from the current PMI exam outline', and masteryexamprep's PMI-PBA syllabus, which cites the PMI-PBA Handbook (revised 24 May 2022) and quotes tasks such as 'Initiate and document requirement changes using agreed change control processes and tooling' and 'Identify acceptance responsibilities (who accepts, evidence required, sign-off process) and align stakeholders'. Neither page quotes PMI's task statements on the requirements baseline; PMI's outline PDF was not opened. The objective wording is the course seed's, to verify. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's pmipba-claims-portal-baseline-signoff (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the business analyst starting a grants management system for a fictional arts foundation. Funders, applicants, assessors and finance all have needs; last time requirements were collected in emails.
handover: The project is predictive with a fixed budget.
Last project: 30% of requirements changed after build started.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.log: Identify stakeholder groups and decision makers.

effects.finding: Four groups; the programme director approves scope; finance owns audit rules.

options.label: A requirements management plan with roles and methods, objective-to-test traceability, and agreed metrics and acceptance criteria

source.note: How long each task takes and when each review or event arrives are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.
How long each task takes and when each review or event arrives are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

then.log: Week 2: assessors and finance send conflicting requirements by email; nobody can say which version is approved.
Week 3: a change to the scoring rules can't be traced; three dependent reports break in testing.
Week 4 (UAT): finance rejects the audit report format; the release slips three weeks.

choices.label: A plan naming stakeholders, roles (who elicits, who approves), elicitation methods per group (workshops, interviews, observation), analysis and approval methods
choices.feedback: The plan sets who does what and how requirements are elicited, analyzed and approved.

choices.label: Use a template from another project unchanged
choices.feedback: It doesn't name this project's stakeholders or approvers.

choices.label: Collect requirements by email as before

tracePrompt.title: How to trace
tracePrompt.context: A spreadsheet or the team's tool?

choices.label: Trace business objectives to requirements, designs and tests in the team's tool with unique IDs and versioning

effects.log: Traceability is defined end to end.

choices.feedback: A traceability strategy links objectives to requirements to tests, versioned.

choices.label: Trace requirements to tests only
choices.feedback: You can't show which objective each requirement serves.

choices.label: Skip traceability: it's overhead
choices.feedback: Changes can't be assessed and delivery can't be evidenced.

accPrompt.title: Who defines done?
accPrompt.context: Last time acceptance was argued at go-live.

choices.label: Define business metrics (grant decisions in 6 weeks, audit findings zero) and acceptance criteria per requirement with each group, approved by the programme director
choices.feedback: Acceptance criteria and metrics defined with stakeholders up front prevent arguments at go-live.

choices.label: Leave acceptance to UAT
choices.feedback: Testing without criteria repeats the go-live arguments.

reflection.question: Write the business analysis plan summary for the programme director.

parts.label: Plan and traceability
parts.criteria: Roles, elicitation and approval methods; traceability from objectives to tests.
parts.modelAnswer: The plan names who elicits and approves, the methods per group, and traces objectives to requirements to tests.

parts.label: Acceptance
parts.criteria: Metrics and criteria agreed with each group.
parts.modelAnswer: Grant decisions in 6 weeks and zero audit findings are the metrics; each requirement has agreed acceptance criteria.

source.note: No risk above appetite at the close without a treatment.
Each key stakeholder at 6 of 10 or more at the close.
